tagline: Aktau on the Caspian — Kazakhstan's seafront city, its Mangystau resort coast, and the eastern anchor of the trans-Caspian corridor.
summary: Kazakhstan's marine-mobility opportunity is its Caspian coast in the Mangystau region, centred on Aktau, the country's only seaport city, with the new port of Kuryk to the south, the Kenderli resort zone and the Bautino/Fort-Shevchenko peninsula to the north. The Caspian here is a tideless, sheltered sea, and Aktau's seafront and the Mangystau resort coast are oriented to the water. Across the sea, Kuryk and Aktau anchor the strategic trans-Caspian crossing to Baku. It is a seafront-and-resort market with a long-haul Quanta-LR corridor dimension.
why_marine_mobility: Kazakhstan's Caspian coast strings Aktau, Kuryk and the Mangystau resort capes along a tideless sea where the coastal road is long but the water is direct. Navier's Pioneer II flies the seafront and resort hops — Aktau to Kuryk, to the Kenderli resort zone and the Bautino peninsula — silent and zero-emission, while the Quanta-LR's hybrid range anchors the eastern end of the strategic trans-Caspian crossing to Baku that no all-electric boat can reach.

demand_signals.label: Aktau seaport city
demand_signals.note: Aktau is Kazakhstan's only seaport city and the Mangystau regional hub, with a seafront oriented to the Caspian and the new port of Kuryk close to the south.

demand_signals.label: Mangystau resort coast
demand_signals.note: The Kenderli resort zone and the Caspian capes draw a growing domestic leisure market along a scenic, sheltered coast.

demand_signals.label: Trans-Caspian corridor
demand_signals.note: Kuryk and Aktau anchor the strategic Caspian crossing to Baku (Alat) — a Middle Corridor trade-and-travel link today served by slow cargo-and-rail ferries.

use_cases.body: A clean foiling tier along the Mangystau seafront — Aktau to Kuryk and the Bautino/Fort-Shevchenko peninsula — on the calm, tideless Caspian.
Resort runs to the Kenderli zone and the Caspian capes for the growing domestic leisure market.
The eastern end of the trans-Caspian passenger crossing to Baku on the Quanta-LR, where the hybrid range handles the long open-sea distance.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The Mangystau seafront-and-resort mesh — Aktau↔Kuryk (~35 nm), Aktau↔Bautino/Fort-Shevchenko (~55 nm), Aktau↔Kenderli (~65 nm, near the upper envelope) — sits within the 70 nm all-electric range on the calm, tideless Caspian off Aktau's seaport and seafront.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The seafront network is Pioneer II territory; the trans-Caspian crossings — Kuryk↔Baku (Alat) (~215 nm) and Aktau↔Baku (~230 nm) — are long-haul Quanta-LR hybrid corridors (H2 2026+) far beyond all-electric range, where the hybrid drivetrain is essential.

transit_planning: For the ports of Aktau and Kuryk (KTZ / national operator) or a Mangystau regional authority: a clean seafront-and-resort tier and the eastern anchor of the trans-Caspian passenger corridor on the Quanta-LR, integrated with the Middle Corridor and Caspian-development strategy.
competitive_landscape: The Mangystau coast has no scheduled coastal passenger water transport — movement is by long coastal road — and the trans-Caspian crossings run on slow cargo-and-rail ferries. There is no foiling tier on either the seafront or the corridors, leaving greenfield room on the calm Caspian.
regulatory_note: Maritime activity falls under the ports of Aktau and Kuryk and Kazakhstan's maritime administration (KTZ), with the Caspian a tideless, sheltered inland sea simplifying near-shore operation. Trans-Caspian crossings involve bilateral coordination with Azerbaijan. Kazakhstan's Middle Corridor and Caspian-development priorities support a clean coastal and corridor tier.
seasonality: The tideless Caspian gives a stable near-shore profile; the Mangystau resort-and-leisure peak is the warm May–September season, while autumn and winter bring strong Caspian winds and occasional northern ice that concentrate near-shore service on the warmer months. The trans-Caspian corridors run year-round.
